Reddit post, r/houseplants.
Title: Croton has wilting leaves after repotting

I have repotted my Croton 10 days ago after noticing, that the soil it was in wasn’t really absorbing any water and bottom leaves drying out and dropping every week or so.

It was doing fine, but I noticed yesterday, that leaves started to wilt and I am unsure what to do.

The soil I used this time is 1:1:1 potting soil (fertilized), leca and pine barks.

What I noticed is, that the soil is quite wet (s. Last photo, watering indicator is fully blue) even though I watered last when I repotted the plant (10 days ago).

No, it was in the soil i bought it in before, which clearly wasn’t taking in any water and the plant was losing a bottom leave every 1-2 weeks.

I have humidifiers at home, humidity is about 50% usually

What is wrong with my plant?
answer:
**Most likely cause: the roots are stressed and the soil is staying too wet.** Repotting damages some roots, and a Croton with damaged roots can't move water up to the leaves, so it wilts even in wet soil. Ten days of wet soil with only one watering suggests the mix or pot is holding water. The old soil was probably compacted or water-repellent, which is why the plant was dropping leaves before, but it doesn't mean the new mix is right. The meter can also read high in a mix with leca and bark, so verify it by hand.

**What to do:**

1. **Stop watering and check the soil by hand.** Push a finger 3 cm into the mix. If it's damp or cold, leave it alone. Lift the pot too, since a heavy pot means water is trapped. Empty any standing water from the decorative basket.
2. **Check the roots if the soil is wet all the way down.** Slide the plant out and look at the roots. Firm white or tan roots are fine. If you find brown, mushy roots with a bad smell, trim them off with clean scissors dipped in rubbing alcohol, and let the plant dry out in fresh, fast-draining mix.
3. **Keep it in bright indirect light at room temperature**, away from heaters and drafts. Don't add extra fertilizer while it recovers.
4. **Water only when the top 3 cm feels dry**, and water thoroughly until it drains. Check again in a week. Expect a few more leaves to drop while it adjusts.
